summary: Polk County, Texas lookout about 2.5 miles south of Camden; stood over a 1935 survey station and was torn down by 1949, leaving concrete footings.

facts.design: Lookout house on a tower, with concrete footings and anchor bolts (1935 survey description)
facts.status_note: Torn down by 1949; only the concrete footings remained according to the survey recovery note.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station; a lookout tower stood over it.
Survey recovery note records the tower as torn down by 1949. The exact date is not given.

evidence.supports: Station about 2.5 miles south of the village of Camden, on a thickly wooded hill

notes_for_editor: One detailed source for the tower: the NGS station description and 1949 recovery note, transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page. I did not open the NGS datasheet (PID BL0723). Not verified that the NGS station (about 2.5 miles south of the village) is the same point as the FFLA coordinates 30.92204, -94.73337. No agency, build date, staffing or access source found. Searches found no lookout-specific history; the TSHA entry covers only the town. Lead for the editor, not used: a November 1930 Texas Forest Service note on cooperative protection in Polk, Tyler, Hardin and Liberty counties mentions two steel towers but names no site (on the Texas page of the Forest Lookouts site).
